verses.sanskrit: मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी | द्रवउ सो दसरथ अजिर बिहारी ||
verses.wordMeaning: The invocation of Tulsidas is not merely ritual — it is a statement of purpose. "Mangal bhavan amangal hari" is one of the most recited Ramcharitmanas lines. Auspiciousness is not luck; it is the natural state when aligned with dharma and when the mind turns toward the divine.
verses.transliteration: maṃgala bhavana amaṃgala hārī | dravau so dasaratha ajira bihārī ||
verses.translation: May He who is the abode of auspiciousness and the destroyer of inauspiciousness — who plays in the courtyard of Dasharatha — be gracious to us.
verses.hindi: जो मंगल का भवन हैं और अमंगल को हरने वाले हैं, जो दशरथ के आँगन में विहार करते हैं — वे (श्री राम) हम पर कृपा करें।
verses.commentary: The invocation of Tulsidas is not merely ritual — it is a statement of purpose. "Mangal bhavan amangal hari" is one of the most recited Ramcharitmanas lines. Auspiciousness is not luck; it is the natural state when aligned with dharma and when the mind turns toward the divine.
verses.science: जो मंगल का भवन हैं और अमंगल को हरने वाले हैं, जो दशरथ के आँगन में विहार करते हैं — वे (श्री राम) हम पर कृपा करें। श्रद्धा और सुरक्षित लगाव तनाव-प्रतिक्रिया को घटाते हैं। यह पंक्ति उसी आश्रय को अपना विषय बनाती है।

verses.sanskrit: जड़ चेतन गुण दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार | संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ||
verses.wordMeaning: The world contains both good and bad — this is a fact. The question is: what do you extract from it? Tulsidas uses the beautiful metaphor of the mythological swan (hamsa) that can separate milk from water. Saints have developed this faculty of discrimination — seeing the good, learning from the bad, not being contaminated by either.
verses.transliteration: jaḍa cetana guṇa doṣamaya bisva kīnha karatāra | saṃta haṃsa guṇa gahahiṃ paya parihari bāri bikāra ||
verses.translation: The Creator made this world full of both inert matter and conscious beings, full of both virtues and faults. Saints, like swans, take the milk of virtues and leave behind the water of faults.
verses.hindi: करतार (ईश्वर) ने यह जगत जड़-चेतन, गुण-दोषमय बनाया। संत हंस के समान गुण रूपी दूध को ग्रहण करते हैं और दोष रूपी जल को छोड़ देते हैं।

verses.sanskrit: सुनत शबरी भक्ति भावि भयाउ तरसी सुधाउ | प्रेम प्रगट सोई जानि भगति न भजति गाउ ||
verses.wordMeaning: The Shabari episode in the Ramcharitmanas is one of Tulsidas's most radical teachings: Shabari, a tribal woman of low caste, offers Rama half-eaten berries she has first tasted herself to ensure they are sweet. Rama accepts them with joy. This overturns all ritual purity rules: what matters is not the ritual correctness of the offering but the love behind it. Tulsidas declares that love (prema) alone is true bhakti.
verses.transliteration: sunata śabarī bhakti bhāvī bhayāu tarasī sudhāu | prema pragaṭa soī jānī bhagati na bhajati gāu ||
verses.translation: Hearing Shabari's devotion, Rama was moved to tears. Knowing that love alone is true devotion, he does not worship without love.
verses.hindi: शबरी की भक्ति सुनकर राम आँसू बहाने लगे। प्रेम ही सच्ची भक्ति जानकर, वे प्रेम के बिना पूजा नहीं करते।

verses.sanskrit: कहँ रघुपति निसिचर भरोसी जोर जोर सुनाउ | जेहि बिधि बिसरहिं सब गति बिसराउ मोर पग चलाउ ||
verses.wordMeaning: The Ram Setu episode: Rama commands the ocean to make way. When the ocean refuses, Rama prepares to dry it up with his arrow. The ocean then surrenders. This is not merely a story of supernatural power — it is a teaching on determination and the divine will. Rama's approach to obstacles is not passive acceptance but active engagement with the world as dharma requires.
verses.transliteration: kahaṃ raghupati nisicara bharosī jora jora sunāu | jehi bidhi bisarihaṃ sab gati bisarāu mora paga calāu ||
verses.translation: Lord Rama said to the ocean with force: hear my command. By whatever means you forget all paths, forget my path and let me cross.
verses.hindi: रघुपति ने समुद्र से ज़ोर से कहा: मेरी बात सुनो। जिस विधि से तुम सब रास्ते भूल जाओ, मेरा रास्ता भूल जाओ और मुझे पार कर दो।

verses.sanskrit: जानकी राम लखन समेत हनुमान | सेवक समेत सब कोटि राम भगवान ||
verses.wordMeaning: A verse from the Ramcharitmanas that declares the multiplicity of Rama: Janki, Rama, Lakshman, Hanuman, and all servants — all are Rama, all are Bhagavan. This is the non-dual heart of Tulsidas's bhakti: the devotee IS the divine. The distinction between servant and Lord dissolves in recognition. Hanuman, the perfect servant, is himself Rama. This is the paradox of bhakti: the more you surrender, the more you become the one you surrender to.
verses.transliteration: jānakī rāma lakhaṇa sameta hanumāna | sevaka sameta saba koṭi rāma bhagavān ||
verses.translation: Janki, Rama, Lakshman, and Hanuman together — with all servants, crores of Rama are the Lord.
verses.hindi: जानकी, राम, लखन और हनुमान साथ में — सेवक समेत सब कोटि राम भगवान हैं।

verses.sanskrit: सुनहु मातु सोइ धनु धन्य | कोइ कोटि करि अपराध न मानु ||
verses.wordMeaning: Rama's response to Kaikeyi — the woman whose demand has just stripped him of everything. He addresses her as "mother" and speaks of inner wealth: the kind of inner abundance in which no outer slight can disturb the peace. This is not weakness; it is the deepest strength — sthitaprajnata (steadiness of wisdom) which the Gita describes and which Rama lives. The Ayodhya Kanda is where Rama earns the title Maryada Purushottama.
verses.transliteration: sunahu mātu soi dhanu dhanya | koi koṭi kari aparādha na mānu ||
verses.translation: Listen, mother — that wealth alone is blessed which makes one not feel offended even when crores of wrongs are done to him.
verses.hindi: सुनो माता! वही धन धन्य है जिसके होते हुए कोई करोड़ों अपराध करे तो भी मन में बुरा न लगे।

verses.sanskrit: एक घड़ी आधी घड़ी आधी में पुनि आध | तुलसी संगत साधु की हरे कोटि अपराध ||
verses.wordMeaning: Satsang — the company of truth-seekers and the wise — is one of the most powerful spiritual technologies across all traditions. Even a moment of genuine contact with a person of wisdom, authentic presence, or elevated consciousness can shift one's inner state in ways that hours of solo practice cannot.
verses.transliteration: eka ghaṛī ādhī ghaṛī ādhī meṃ puni ādha | tulasī saṃgata sādhu kī hare koṭi aparādha ||
verses.translation: One moment, half a moment, or even half of half a moment — Tulsidas says the company of the holy eradicates crores of sins.
verses.hindi: एक घड़ी, आधी घड़ी, या आधी में भी आधी — तुलसीदास कहते हैं कि साधु की संगति करोड़ों अपराधों को नष्ट कर देती है।

verses.sanskrit: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी | तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी ||
verses.wordMeaning: Tulsidas defines friendship by a single quality: responsiveness to a friend's pain. verses.transliteration: je na mitra dukha hohiṃ dukhārī | tinhahi bilokata pātaka bhārī ||
verses.translation: Those who do not grieve at a friend's sorrow — merely beholding them is a great sin.
verses.hindi: जो मित्र के दुख में दुखी नहीं होते — उन्हें देखना भी महापाप है।

verses.translation: A wicked servant, a wicked enemy's wife, a wicked enemy — all three are to be subdued by the door of wisdom.
verses.hindi: दुष्ट सेवक, शत्रु की स्त्री, और दुष्ट शत्रु — इन तीनों को विवेक के द्वार से ही जीता जाता है।

verses.sanskrit: जड़ चेतन गुण दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार | संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ||
verses.wordMeaning: The world contains both good and bad — this is a fact. The question is: what do you extract from it? Tulsidas uses the beautiful metaphor of the mythological swan (hamsa) that can separate milk from water. Saints have developed this faculty of discrimination — seeing the good, learning from the bad, not being contaminated by either.

verses.translation: The Creator made this world full of both inert matter and conscious beings, full of both virtues and faults. Saints, like swans, take the milk of virtues and leave behind the water of faults.
verses.hindi: करतार (ईश्वर) ने यह जगत जड़-चेतन, गुण-दोषमय बनाया। संत हंस के समान गुण रूपी दूध को ग्रहण करते हैं और दोष रूपी जल को छोड़ देते हैं।

verses.sanskrit: काम क्रोध मद लोभ सब नाथ नरक के पन्थ | सब परिहरि रघुबीरहि भजहु भजहु भव दन्थ ||

verses.transliteration: kāma krodha mada lobha saba nātha naraka ke pantha | saba parihari raghubīrahi bhajahu bhajahu bhava dantha ||
verses.translation: Lust, anger, pride, and greed — O Lord, these are all the paths to hell. Abandon them all and worship Raghuvira — worship Him, the destroyer of the world's pain.
verses.hindi: काम, क्रोध, मद और लोभ — हे प्रभु! ये सब नरक के मार्ग हैं। इन सबको छोड़कर रघुवीर का भजन करो — उनका भजन करो जो संसार के दुखों को दूर करते हैं।

verses.sanskrit: निज दोष कहत न लजाहीं | काहू सो पूछत बनही नाहीं ||
verses.wordMeaning: Tulsidas's sharp observation of spiritual pride: the person who cannot admit fault and cannot ask for help is already lost. Spiritual maturity begins with the willingness to be corrected and the humility to ask for guidance.
verses.transliteration: nija doṣa kahata na lajāhīṃ | kāhū so pūchata banaī nāhīṃ ||
verses.translation: They are not ashamed to speak of their own faults; they cannot bear to ask anyone anything.
verses.hindi: अपने दोष कहते हुए वे लजाते नहीं; किसी से कुछ पूछना उन्हें सुहाता नहीं।

verses.sanskrit: सुनत शबरी भक्ति भावि भयाउ तरसी सुधाउ | प्रेम प्रगट सोई जानि भगति न भजति गाउ ||

verses.hindi: शबरी की भक्ति सुनकर राम आँसू बहाने लगे। प्रेम ही सच्ची भक्ति जानकर, वे प्रेम के बिना पूजा नहीं करते।

verses.wordMeaning: The Ram Setu episode: Rama commands the ocean to make way. When the ocean refuses, Rama prepares to dry it up with his arrow. The ocean then surrenders. This is not merely a story of supernatural power — it is a teaching on determination and the divine will. Rama's approach to obstacles is not passive acceptance but active engagement with the world as dharma requires.

verses.sanskrit: दैहिक दैविक भौतिक तापा | राम राज काहूहि नहिं ब्यापा || सब नर करहिं परस्पर प्रीती | चलहिं स्वधर्म निरत श्रुति नीती ||
verses.wordMeaning: Tulsidas's definition of Ramrajya — not a theocracy, not a specific governance structure, but a condition: the absence of all three forms of suffering (physical illness, natural disasters, and social conflict) combined with the presence of love among all people and faithful performance of one's own role. verses.sanskrit: राम कहत चलु राम कहत चलु राम कहत चलु भाई | जो यह राम नाम रट लावे ताहि न काल सताई ||
verses.wordMeaning: The Uttara Kanda's central bhakti teaching: the Name as the complete practice. verses.translation: Keep saying "Rama," keep saying "Rama," keep saying "Rama," brother. Whoever fixes this name of Rama — time will not torment that one.
verses.hindi: राम कहते चलो, राम कहते चलो, राम कहते चलो, भाई। जो यह राम-नाम जपता रहे — काल भी उसे नहीं सताता।
